Pleasure Island is the island south of Wilmington that holds the towns of Carolina Beach and Kure Beach. Kure Beach describes itself as on Pleasure Island, between Carolina Beach and Fort Fisher, and Fort Fisher sits at the southern end of the island just past Kure Beach.
Is it free to go to the beach at Carolina Beach?

Yes. The Wilmington and Beaches visitors bureau says there is no charge to access the beach at Carolina Beach. Parking is a separate matter: in 2026 paid parking ran March 1 to October 31, 9 a.m. to 8 p.m., and was free November 1 to the end of February. See the parking guide for each beach.
Can I bring my dog to the beach on Pleasure Island?

At Carolina Beach, dogs must be leashed. From April 1 to September 30 they are allowed on the beach only before 9 a.m. and after 5 p.m., and from October 1 to March 31 at any hour. Dogs are not allowed on the historic wooden boardwalk or in the Boardwalk Business District at any time. Rules differ at Kure Beach, so check the town of Kure Beach before you go.
Is Fort Fisher State Historic Site free?

General admission is free and donations are welcome. The site is open Tuesday to Saturday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., and closed Sunday, Monday and designated state holidays. Guided tours cost extra and are sold on site, so call the information desk at 910-251-7351 to confirm which tours run that day.
Is the North Carolina Aquarium at Fort Fisher open?

No, not for now. The aquarium closed to the public on May 26, 2026 for construction that the state expects to take 30 months. The state has not given a reopening date. The Fort Fisher historic site, the state recreation area and the beaches remain open.
Can I get to Pleasure Island by ferry?

Yes. NCDOT runs a vehicle and passenger ferry between Fort Fisher and Southport, with a crossing time of about 35 minutes. Schedules change by season, so check the NCDOT ferry page for the current times before you plan around it.
